quote: I have an excellent credit score. But why would I need credit?
stewart_read: Rep admits ignorance instead of using the tax-credit rationale from the script's disclosure note.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could have deflected to specialist rather than confessing lack of knowledge.
coaching_implication: Use 'that's one of our program requirements, our specialist can explain the why in detail' instead of 'I honestly don't know.'

quote: So the the way the program works, there's no upfront cost, and you don't have to pay for install.
stewart_read: Rep volunteers financial mechanism detail (bill swap) unprompted, closer-tier content that confused rather than reassured.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged a quick reassurance was needed to keep the customer engaged before losing him — but the depth given went well beyond reassurance.
coaching_implication: Redirect with the escape hatch: 'Great question — the specialist walks through exact costs and savings on the design call.'

stewart_read: This is the cost-objection moment where a bill flip ('what's expensive is your current C&T bill') would land better than another mechanics explanation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have believed clarity, not inversion, was needed — reasonable read given the customer's genuine confusion, but the schema move was still available.
coaching_implication: When customer says 'I'm not following,' pivot to the bill-pain flip instead of re-explaining the payment structure a third time.

stewart_read: A $929 bill (annual or on top of the ~$200/mo figure) is a striking anchor point the rep files without reflecting it back for emotional weight.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be saving the number for the specialist to use during the proposal rather than working it live — plausible but unconfirmed by anything said later in the call.
coaching_implication: Reflect big numbers back immediately: 'wow, $929 — that's a lot going to the utility, let's see what solar can replace that with.'

quote: I actually got two electric bills. I got a I got a pool house for my swimming pool too.
stewart_read: A pool house with its own meter signals a larger energy footprint and potential upsell scope, but rep only asks about combining meters, not exploring the pool/energy angle.
coaching_implication: Note the pool house as a usage-driver worth flagging to the design team, not just a meter-consolidation question.

quote: What? The that's on me to show up or what?
stewart_read: Customer is alarmed at an in-person visit; rep quickly offers a phone call alternative, which resolves it, but the initial framing ('they'll come by') created avoidable anxiety.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may not have known the customer's channel preference until asked — reactive, not deliberate, since the offer defaults to in-person first.
coaching_implication: Offer phone vs in-person proactively rather than defaulting to in-person and backpedaling.

quote: I need to know Cox and all that. It's worth well, I'm 73 years old.
stewart_read: Customer discloses age and financial caution as a vulnerability signal; rep responds with generic reassurance about no money down rather than acknowledging the disclosure directly.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the age/caution explicitly ('that makes sense to be careful') before pivoting to the no-money-down reassurance.

quote: It's got my text people down here, but I don't I'm not sure how to add one or how to put you in there.
stewart_read: Customer struggles with Android photo-share for over two minutes; schema calls for a verbal read-back pivot within 2 minutes, which the rep didn't use.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the photo was close to landing and worth pushing through given the customer had already found the share menu — a defensible in-the-moment call given how close the resolution was.
coaching_implication: Set a 2-minute timer mentally on tech friction; pivot to 'just read me the kWh numbers off the bar graph' if no progress.
